Lists and tuples are both sequences in Python. The main difference is that lists are mutable and tuples are immutable. Lists use square brackets and tuples use parentheses. Because tuples are immutable, they are hashable and can be used as dictionary keys, whereas lists cannot. Tuples also have a slight memory and performance advantage. Use lists when you need a collection that changes, like a shopping cart. Use tuples for fixed collections, like coordinates or function return values.

Overfitting is when your model performs well on training data but poorly on new data. It basically memorizes the training set instead of learning general patterns. You can detect it when training accuracy is high but validation accuracy is much lower. To prevent overfitting, you can use cross-validation to get a better estimate of model performance, apply regularization like L1 or L2 to penalize complex models, use dropout in neural networks, implement early stopping to halt training when validation performance degrades, collect more training data, and use feature selection to remove irrelevant features. The fundamental idea is managing the bias-variance tradeoff by finding the right model complexity for your data size.

Precision is about being correct when you predict positive. Recall is about finding all the positives. F1 is the average of both. High precision is important when false positives are bad, like spam detection. High recall is important when missing positives is dangerous, like cancer detection. You calculate F1 as two times precision times recall divided by precision plus recall. They are more useful than accuracy when classes are imbalanced.

An INNER JOIN returns only rows that have matching values in both tables. For example, if you join a customers table with an orders table on customer_id, only customers who have placed orders will appear in the result. A LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and the matched rows from the right table. Customers without orders would still appear, but with NULL values in the order columns. LEFT JOIN is useful for finding records without corresponding entries, like customers who have never ordered. INNER JOIN generally produces smaller result sets and can be more performant, but the choice should be driven by what the query needs to answer, not performance alone.
